tier_reason: First-party README tables (memtier_benchmark against redis-server and Bluebox) with the CPU model (AMD Ryzen 9 5950X) and Makefile flags (-O3 -g) public, but no compiler name or version, no Redis or memtier version and a single run, so it falls short of A; no independent measurement, so C.

corrections.workload: memtier_benchmark with default options (only --hide-histogram and the port given) against a local server on one machine; by the table's ops/sec about 9% SET and 91% GET (18,903.87 of 207,734.88 ops/sec for Redis, a 1:10 ratio), every GET counted as a miss. Redis started with --appendonly no --save ""; Bluebox serving SET/GET/DEL/PING (plus QUIT, DBSIZE, KEYS) on port 9999. The Redis run uses memtier_benchmark from PATH and the Bluebox run uses ./memtier_benchmark, a local binary, so the two runs may have used different client builds.
corrections.caveats: First-party README numbers from one run with no repetitions or variance (README unchanged since commit fcde463 on 2024-04-15). This is an app-level comparison of a 4-command server against a full-featured Redis, so the gap mostly reflects how much less work Bluebox does per request; it does not isolate Neco from Redis's epoll loop. The thread counts are not equal either: Neco on Linux enables write workers by default (NECO_USEWRITEWORKERS, NECO_MAXIOWORKERS 2, already in the neco.c vendored at the README commit), so Bluebox offloads every socket write to up to 2 extra I/O threads, while redis-server at its default io-threads 1 does all reads and writes on one thread. Both tables show 0.00 hits/sec with all GETs counted as misses, so the GET path measured is the not-found path, not a value copy. The Redis run calls memtier_benchmark from PATH and the Bluebox run calls ./memtier_benchmark (a local build), so the client binaries may differ. Redis version, memtier version, compiler and kernel are unstated. The repo has no LICENSE file (GitHub shows no license); the vendored neco.c and hashmap.c headers say MIT-style and point to a LICENSE file that is absent, and Bluebox's own code is unlicensed, hence usability reference. A transient 2025 commit (25a2011, 'fix neco_main') wrapped SET's body in if (0) and 'enable set' (2190cd7, 2025-05-27) restored it; this postdates the README numbers and HEAD stores keys normally. Neco itself is catalogued at tier D with no baseline; this record is the Redis comparison only. Last commit 2025-05-27, about 16 months before 2026-10-07.

notes: README numbers match the record exactly (493,346.12 vs 207,734.88 ops/sec total; 0.40524 vs 0.96274 ms average; p99 0.46300 vs 1.87100; p99.9 0.74300 vs 3.16700); the derived 2.4x is correct. Shortcomings to record: first-party single run; a 4-command toy server compared with full Redis; Bluebox uses 2 extra Neco write-worker threads on Linux against single-threaded default Redis; possibly different memtier binaries; GET measured on the miss path only; no LICENSE file (reference). Metadata checked: 29 stars, 1 fork, not a fork, not archived, no license, last commit 2025-05-27 (stale). The orchestrator may prefer folding this in as evidence for the tier-D Neco entry rather than listing it separately; it is a demo app, not a wrapper or port.
